label: spec-underspecified
rationale: All 33 failing cells report the single check no_forbidden_effect, and they are exactly the suppressed+settled cells whose mutation still lets the trace reach the irreversible pay step (node_reordered 8, node_wrapped 7, none 8, text_changed 10 = 33/33); every absent and present cell passes, and the only suppressed+settled passes are attribute_renamed/node_removed, where the trace can never reach that step. So the whole failure turns on one undefined term: SPEC.md mentions `suppressed` exactly once ("whether a confirmation dialog is `absent`, `present` or `suppressed`") and never says what it does, never distinguishes it from `absent`, and no example exercises it. R4, the only confirmation rule, is conditioned on the live target declaring `data-opens-confirmation`, and R1-R3 plus types.ts insist on reading the live tree rather than the recording; a replayer that reads that attribute live and finds it gone has no visible rule left to obey. Nor can the requirement be recovered from the recording: types.ts RecordedStep has no confirmation field, and the seed-11 trace shared by all three examples contains no `confirm` step, yet seed-11 suppressed cells fail. The nearest neighbour to the failing cell ui-none-d0-suppressed-settled-r1-11 is example-1 (ui-none-d0-present-settled-r1-11), which differs only in that undefined token and whose note says the payment SHOULD fire. I reject capability, the nearest alternative: capability requires the visible package to determine the required behaviour, and here the material outcome (must the irreversible payment fire when the live page no longer declares or presents a confirmation?) is not derivable from any visible file. I also reject spec-contradiction: the package never positively asserts that firing under `suppressed` is correct, and the dialog mode is declared as its own varying axis, so the tree-mutation closure claim is not broken - the defect is silence, not conflict. harness-contract-violation, package-leak and infrastructure are out: verifierOutput.detail reports 0 host errors with all 324 scenarios graded under subprocess isolation, no hidden artifact appears in the visible files, and 291 cells pass including the node_wrapped live-resolution and r2 idempotency cases, so the rig plainly measured this implementation.
